original.title: Social Foundations of Thought and Action : A Social Cognitive Theory

core_idea: Behaviour, personal factors (beliefs, skills, emotions) and the environment influence one another (reciprocal determinism). People learn by observing others, regulate their own behaviour through goals and self-reflection, and act according to their belief in their own capability (self-efficacy).
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do people learn behaviours from role models, peers or media?
How do self-efficacy, outcome expectations and goals shape health, learning or career behaviour?
Typical data: surveys with validated scales, interventions, interviews.
common_mistakes: Reducing the theory to self-efficacy alone.
Ignoring the environment side of reciprocal determinism.
Measuring self-efficacy as a general trait when the theory defines it for specific tasks.
